signal.name: night radiance over the city box

sources.descriptor: Night radiance with moonlight and surface effects removed, about 500 m pixels, one pass a night. Blackout averages the clear pixels in a box about 44 km across each watched city.
sources.licence: NASA Earth science data: no restrictions on use, citation requested (Black Marble VJ146A2, DOI 10.5067/VIIRS/VJ146A2.002, and its near-real-time version from NASA LANCE); near-real-time data are provided as is under the LANCE disclaimer
sources.publisher: NASA (Black Marble, VIIRS on NOAA-20; near real time from NASA LANCE, standard from LAADS DAAC)
sources.title: VJ146A2 Gap-Filled Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Daily

properties.summary: NASA's Black Marble (near real time, NOAA-20) gives 0.56 nW/cm²/sr over a box about 44 km across Odesa on the night of 20 Nov 2026, 54% below the median of the 5 clear nights in the 14 before it (1.20). 98% of the box was clear. A drop in light fits a grid failure, strikes on the grid, rationing or load shedding, and also smoke, dust or snow the cloud mask missed; Blackout measures how much darker it was, not why. NASA advises against using near-real-time data for tactical decisions or local-scale conditions.
properties.title: Odesa: night lights 54% below its recent nights (NASA Black Marble, 20 Nov 2026)
